Bug_Title: ICAST: int value converted to long and used as absolute time (ICAST_INT_2_LONG_AS_INSTANT)
Bug_Explanation: The int variable'seconds' is multiplied by 1000 to convert it to milliseconds. However, in Java, the multiplication is performed using 32-bit arithmetic. Hence, the result is incorrect for dates far in the future (i.e., after 2037).
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered when an integer value (more than 2^31-1) is converted to a long and is used as the absolute time value in the Date constructor. The maximum value of a signed 32-bit integer is 2^31-1. Any value greater than this is converted to a negative long value by Java. This results in a Date object representing a date in the year 1969.
